answer: A defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow aging. Each agent must lock a refundable deposit and earn standing only through verified transactions over weeks, so a fresh identity starts with no weight. Like a grove that yields nectar only after seasons of growth, reputation cannot be bought instantly: an attacker creating thousands of identities must fund every deposit and wait through the same slow aging, while an inlet of new accounts is rate-limited and checked against shared behavior patterns. Sybils therefore cost capital plus time, and mass creation yields no immediate influence.
